title: The True Kick-and-Flee
text: I had fragmentary memories from a loop that had lingered in Melromarc… that thing has been parasitic on me since way back then, I say. Not even eliminating the spirit of the spear takes care of it—what an extraordinarily troublesome creature. So I had Father borrow the shed where the meat of the Dimensional Chimera gets delivered, and arranged for Filo-tan to rest there.

Of course, I remembered all this from my loop memories, indeed. I couldn’t possibly forget the memory of the loop where I finally managed to reunite with Filo-tan. Here, Sakura-chan—who would become Filo-tan—occasionally tore off bits of chimera meat and ate them, I say. And now, it was time to carry out the next necessary action.

So, with that in mind, I brought Rabbit Guy along and casually made my way to the fondly remembered scene where Filo-tan kicks someone. Compared to my memory, Father and the others arrived a bit late, but sure enough, here came the Filolial-sama pulling the cart—surely Filo-tan—along with Father and Older Sister.

Ah… what a nostalgic sight, I say. Come to think of it, I can’t quite recall why I laughed so hard back then. Somehow the sight of a vaguely irritated Father, the cart, and Filo-tan struck some mysterious funny bone in me and set me off into fits of laughter.
“So, I just need to laugh at Iwatani-sama and the others over there?”
“Shh! They’ll hear you. Laugh without confirming anything first. Do it with convincing acting so they don’t catch on, I say.”
“Haah… why do I have to play this role…”
And so, as Filo-tan cheerfully trotted along pulling the cart, Rabbit Guy pointed at her and gradually approached while bursting into exaggerated laughter, indeed.
“Pfft! What is that! Haha, oh no, this is hitting my funny bone! Bwahaha! Wahahahahahaha!”
It was a bit overacted, but Rabbit Guy pointed at Filo-tan and Father exactly as I’d instructed.
“Ohh my.”
Older Sister watched the scene with a cheerful smile.
“…What’s with you two all of a sudden.”

Ah, that listless look on Father’s face from back then comes flooding back. Since I’d asked him to, he obliged by glaring at us with visible irritation. Later, Father would tell me, “It really pained me to put on that little farce with everyone…” At the same time, his eyes seemed to be asking—wait, Rabbit Guy is playing this role? Is that really okay?
“B-Because! It’s so tasteless, isn’t it!”
“What is?”
Later, Rabbit Guy told me he genuinely couldn’t understand pointing at such an ordinary sight and calling it tasteless.
“Are you planning to peddle goods or something? Poor people sure have it rough. And honestly, what a lame-looking Filolial!”

“Gyahahaha!” Rabbit Guy performed, thoroughly in character. He’d gotten quite used to this. Incidentally, it was after this that Father, in the original world, started peddling goods. When I told Father about this episode later…
“Maybe when Motoyasu-kun said that to me, it planted the idea that peddling might not be a bad option.”
…was what he said. What, so my remark was what set him on that path? Knowing that made the truth rather pleasing to me. And the important thing here, apparently, was this:

“Basically, I think the key was mocking her appearance. From what you told me, Motoyasu-kun, it sounds like Sakura-chan and Filo-chan look different enough in the face that you could mistake them for entirely different people. I bet getting laughed at for her looks made her picture an appearance that would be found cute when she eventually turned into her angel form.”
…is what he told me. So apparently, I had to mock Filo-tan here. No doubt the Crimson Swine had also hurled plenty of unnecessary insults back then too.

“How pathetic! A horse—no wait, not a griffin, a Filolial, and what’s with this color, it’s supposed to be white but it’s a washed-out pink! If it’s going to be white, it should be pure white! And way too slow on top of that!”
“…I don’t get what’s so funny about any of this.”

Father answered in a tone that sounded thoroughly exasperated with Rabbit Guy’s attitude. Now then! Hurry up and get closer, I say! I won’t allow any dodging. Just to be safe, I gave Rabbit Guy a little jab with a Slow Spear for its slowing effect, then discreetly pushed his back to send him toward Filo-tan. Rabbit Guy, still pointing at Filo-tan, drifted closer.
“Guaaaaa!”

And with that, Filo-tan spread her wings and sent Rabbit Guy flying with a kick, I say. Yes! Excellent! Rabbit Guy sailed roughly three meters through the air, his laughing expression still frozen on his face. A direct hit to the family jewels, indeed. Damn… he didn’t fly as far as I did. Must be the effect of the enhancement. I felt a bit uneasy—was he going to be okay?
“Ugwoooohh… the culprit is—o—”
“Kyaaaaaaaa! Rabbit Guuuuuy!”
I mimicked the sort of line the Crimson Swine would say. Father nearly stumbled and fell over—was he all right!?
“Guaaaaaaaaaa!”

Filo-tan, huffing with indignation, took off running, pulling the cart with Father and Older Sister aboard. It was over in an instant. If I chased after her, I’d catch up easily enough, but… was that already Filo-tan? When I chased her down after restarting the loop before, she did indeed turn into Filo-tan for me. But just to be extra careful, I’d been told to trace the same steps until she transformed into her angel form, so I decided to hold back.
“Well done accomplishing your task, Rabbit Guy.”
“Ugh… I tried to dodge at the last second, but you did something, didn’t you. Everything around me suddenly sped up terrifyingly fast, it startled me!”
Twitching and convulsing where he lay sprawled on the ground, Rabbit Guy lodged his complaint at me.
“I won’t tolerate any unnecessary tricks from you, indeed. Regardless, well done accomplishing your task!”

I bestowed my praise upon him. So naturally, I had to administer proper treatment. Be grateful for my mercy, I say. Well, I’m no match for Father, but I’m no slouch with healing magic myself, indeed. And so, I healed the spot where Filo-tan’s kick had landed on Rabbit Guy. Thanks to the enhancement effect he’d gone flying, but it wasn’t a serious injury.
“More importantly, what was with that creepy scream just now!”
“That was as faithful a reproduction as I could manage, I say.”
“Ugh, honestly. I have no idea what’s going on anymore. Try being the one who has to laugh hysterically at an everyday sight for once!”
“This too was a matter of great importance, indeed. And also, consider it a bit of punishment for how full of yourself you’ve been getting lately. This should settle the score.”
“I’m going to hold a grudge over this, you know!”
“Hahaha! No idea what you’re talking about.”

Regardless of everything, by tomorrow evening I’d finally get to see Filo-tan again! And so, the reunion with Filo-tan, along with the experiment to establish a method for meeting her in future loops, had reached its final phase. Since it was certain Father would come to the monster dealer’s tent by the following afternoon, we made sure to thoroughly eliminate our scent and finished evacuating to the circus tent. Up to this point, everything had gone off without a hitch, indeed. What flickered across my mind, though, was that mysterious entity the spirit of the spear had introduced… right up until I encountered it.
“Well now… I came to see what all the fuss was about, and all I can say is I’m astonished. Yes indeed.”

I’d arranged for the monster dealer to play along with the script too. Everything was proceeding exactly as scripted. Filo-tan, now in her Filolial Queen form, was brought to the monster dealer’s tent by Father, indeed.
“Kweh?”
Filo-tan tilted her head to one side, indeed.
“…So, I want to ask you honestly. This thing hatched from an egg I bought from your shop, but what exactly did you sell me?”
Acting like I didn’t know something I understood perfectly well was quite the ordeal, let me tell you.
“Kweeeh?”
Filo-tan glanced around at her surroundings, looking this way and that.
Father, too, seemed to be scanning the area, searching for me. From within my cloaking, I gently took hold of his hand.
“Ohh my.”

Older Sister, seeming to understand perfectly well what was going on, wore a mischievous little smile. But Father, even as he offered a faint smile, seemed to make an expression as though something felt slightly off. Whatever could that have been about, I wonder?
